**Answer: why mise refuses direnv support**

The refusal is **both principled (real technical conflict) and territorial (product-direction choice)** — and jdx (Jeff Dickey, the BDFL; no other maintainer has a distinct published position) has said so more or less explicitly.

**Maintainers' core arguments, in jdx's own words:**
- Current policy (https://mise.jdx.dev/direnv.html): "Using direnv with mise is unsupported. Compatibility issues are not considered mise bugs, and PRs for direnv compatibility are not accepted. The `use mise` integration is deprecated."
- On the deprecation PR (https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/3464, Dec 11 2024): "this is not a new decision, this simply documents what has been the actual state of the world for a long time… I'm probably willing to accept PRs for it too, so it's kind of a 'soft' deprecation. I won't be maintaining it myself… And using direnv with mise together is something I'm going to be more explicit about not supporting."
- On direction (mise-docs archive, Jan 21 2024, https://github.com/jdx/mise-docs/blob/HEAD/direnv.md): "The project direction of mise has changed… the new direction is for it to be capable of replacing direnv completely for any use-case… Not because it's a maintenance burden, but because it just hasn't seemed like a particularly useful solution and it may help focus mise on the functionality that does work for users."

**Technical conflict (real):** Both tools hook chpwd/precmd and snapshot/restore the env. The docs: "Their shell hooks can disagree about which PATH entries to add, restore, or remove." direnv records before/after env in `DIRENV_DIFF` (base64+zlib JSON) and deletes unrecognized PATH entries on the next hook run; mise's `src/direnv.rs` (read live at https://github.com/jdx/mise/blob/main/src/direnv.rs) fights back with `add_path_to_old_and_new`, commented: "the purpose is to trick direnv into thinking that this path has always been there… that way it does not remove it when it modifies PATH." Concrete bugs: #70 (mise cleared the entire PATH when PATH wasn't in DIRENV_DIFF, fixed PR #73 https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/73), the unload PATH-reset e2e test (PR #79), and issue #2362 (https://github.com/jdx/mise/issues/2362) where `use mise` + `source .venv/bin/activate` caused venvs to be "randomly deactivated" mid-session — the report that triggered formal deprecation.

**Deprecation timeline:**
- Jan 2023: PR #23 adds `use mise` as a stopgap ("Direnv isn't compatible with `rtx activate`… in the meantime…").
- Jan 2024: jdx floats deprecation; direction = replace direnv; admits `use mise` had "virtually no reports of problems."
- Dec 11, 2024: PR #3464 / commit 816d6ee formally deprecates (closes #2362), hides `mise direnv activate` from CLI docs — a self-described "soft" deprecation.
- Apr 10, 2026: commit ca78346 hardens to "PRs to improve direnv compatibility will not be accepted," removing the earlier "open an issue so we can close those gaps" and "compatibility will always be a major goal" language. (https://github.com/jdx/mise/commit/ca7834674fe5a926f462e9c65bb748f8cc0f2ccc)
- Apr 2026: community PR #8857 (empty-DIRENV_DIFF parse fix) still merged — minor robustness fixes land even under the hard policy.

**Legitimate coexistence:** the docs concede simple cases work — direnv for *unrelated* env vars / unrelated PATH additions, mise for tool versions; never let both manage the same runtime or venv (direnv `layout python` vs mise python is the canonical conflict). Maintainer-endorsed venv answer is mise-native `_.python.venv` / `python.uv_venv_auto`.

**Community workarounds:** nix-community/home-manager's `programs.direnv.mise.enable` keeps the deprecated integration alive by shipping `eval "$(mise direnv activate)"` into `~/.config/direnv/lib/hm-mise.sh` (https://github.com/nix-community/home-manager/blob/master/modules/programs/direnv.nix); at least one user deliberately keeps `use_mise` (perf: one-shot per cd vs `hook-env` per prompt); the old docs' escape hatch of driving mise via `MISE_*` env vars in `.envrc` with no hooks. No fork of mise itself for direnv exists.

**Assessment:** principled *and* territorial. The PATH hook fight is genuine (bugs + falsified-diff hacks prove it), but the Apr 2026 "PRs not accepted" hardening goes beyond what the technical facts required — jdx himself called `use mise` "surprisingly stable" and was open to PRs in 2024. The hard line is a focus/strategy decision: mise intends to replace direnv, not coexist with it.

**Could not verify:** authorship of the #2362 thread comment "you probably just shouldn't use direnv and mise for venvs together" (page extraction didn't attribute comments); exact diff of the companion Apr 2026 commit ab140c8 (end state visible in live docs)."
